subject: design-technology
title: Stretch: Stock Forms, Tolerances and Global Production
welcome_lead: Push past the basics into standard stock forms, tolerances and the global flow of materials.
meta_desc: Explore stock forms, tolerances and global supply for GCSE Design & Technology.
final_note: You can specify stock forms, set tolerances and discuss offshoring trade-offs.

walkthroughs.body_html: Timber comes as planks, boards and dowels; metal as sheet, bar, rod and tube; polymer as granules, sheet or film. Using standard stock forms reduces waste and cuts cost because designers cut to size rather than ordering custom blanks.

A shaft labelled 20 mm ± 0.1 must measure between 19.9 and 20.1 mm. Tight tolerances cost more because they need precise tooling. Looser tolerances are fine for parts that do not need to fit precisely.
A UK firm offshores T-shirt printing to cut labour costs by 60%. Later, shipping delays and quality issues push them to reshore. Decisions weigh cost, quality, lead time and ethics.
